inputs.original_text: Cyprus is considering surveillance law changes that would strip away judicial oversight, one of the few safeguards against state power being used without meaningful accountability. Lawyers are raising the alarm, and the amended bill is expected to face a House vote on Thursday. This is not a technical tweak: weakening oversight risks putting people’s privacy and civil liberties at the mercy of institutions with less independent scrutiny. The public deserves transparency and strong protections before any such changes are approved.
inputs.modified_text: Cyprus is moving toward a surveillance law that would weaken judicial oversight, one of the few checks on unchecked state power. Lawyers are warning about the amended bill ahead of a House vote on Thursday, and the stakes go well beyond legal procedure: people with the least power are often most exposed when surveillance operates without independent scrutiny. Privacy and civil liberties cannot depend on institutions policing themselves. The public needs transparency and strong safeguards before this change is approved.
